data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains rather than describes its subject when the subject's failure is made a precondition for testing other subjects, so the test's distribution over mutations is conditional on an arbitrary first failure and the observed 3-of-26 is an artifact of conditioning, not a property of the guarded modules.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If removing the first failing mutation and re-running the remaining 25 yields the same survivors, the conditioning claim is refuted.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 3-of-26 survivors are identical across many different first-failure choices, then the first failure is not conditioning the outcome.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1-of-9 compile.py survivor is killed in a run where the first failure is a compile.py mutation, then the conditioning direction matters and the mechanism is supported.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 4/4-to-6/7 gradient is not monotone in the number of prior failures, the conditioning mechanism is too simple.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The fail-first installation acts as a conditioning operation: the first failing mutation is not measured, it is installed as a filter. The remaining 25 mutations are then tested under a subject that has already been modified to fail, so the test asks 'does this mutation survive given that the subject is already failing?' rather than 'does this mutation fail?'. The 1-of-9 compile.py survival and the 4/4-to-6/7 module scores are then conditional probabilities whose denominator is not the mutation set but the post-first-failure state space.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
